They do not deny knowing novelty of wickedness, but they practice it shamefully, as if they are superior when not caught; for they are full of wickedness, bearing all uncleanness within, and they make a pretense of virtue with the name of fasting alone; for who would say that the most ignorant and uneducated Pharisee, whom our Lord Christ describes in the Gospels as praying in the temple, is not boastful about his fasting and tithing, while being full of pride and uncleanness within, like whitewashed tombs, beautiful on the outside but full of dead bones and all uncleanness within

For they did not want to know the divine law, but also having trampled on the one given to them, they were disobedient and unrepentant. And God reproaches them through the prophet, saying: 'To whom shall I speak and testify, and they will listen? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear.' For the word of the Lord became a mockery to them, and they did not want to hear it. For those who sin voluntarily, the advice of what is beneficial is burdensome. And to those who want to live licentiously, self-control is not pleasant. For just as the mind of those who are drunk is confirmed in foolishness, and right thinking is removed, so those who are conquered by pleasure and have sunk into the depths of sin, having surrendered their sober mind to unclean passions, have evil firmly established within themselves, completely inclined towards it and looking at it, bound by this disease.

From the day your fathers came out of Egypt until this day, I sent all my servants the prophets to you, but they did not listen to me, and they stiffened their necks more than their fathers, and you alone have been shown the evil of your ancestors' deeds, and you have been born in unrighteousness, and you have condemned the weaknesses of the law, and you have been given the power to overcome, but you have chosen victory over all shame, and you have been allotted a vote, but God, the judge of all, condemns you, and they stiffened their necks, and the prophet is told to lament, and the Lord says that he has rejected and despised the generation that did these things, and the sons of Judah did evil in his sight, and they set up abominations in the house that bears his name, and they built the altar of Topheth, and they even denied their benefactor and considered idolatry more useful, and they gave sacrifices to the gods they had created for themselves

Others, being led by their passions, were devoting their minds to foreign desires, and having seized the most beautiful mountain groves, they were offering sacrifices to the demons there, calling upon the nymphs, as it seems to me, according to the poets of the Greeks, Hamadryads and Oreades. And being shameless towards every desire, they were not being restrained, but rather boasting about these things, they were causing great pain to the lawgiver. Therefore, Jeremiah the prophet says: 'You have seen what the house of Israel has done to me; they went up to every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and they committed fornication there. And after they had committed all these fornications, they did not return to me.' For they hate the ways of benefit, by which they are not pleased to be saved, and they do not avoid the time of pleasure, not abstaining from it; but they always extend towards the worse, not knowing how to be self-controlled. The harsh and unyielding choice of the Jews will testify to these things, having neither guarded the beginning nor been humble towards the ambition of the Master.

For if it is possible for them to be saved by knowing, and they have neglected the things that are beneficial, and they have not considered the great love of humanity, how will they not reasonably condemn themselves? For how will they not be found to have gone beyond all arrogance, they who, having the opportunity to find release from punishment, have departed from sin, and have called upon themselves a heavier punishment, always adding to their transgressions? To those who are disposed in this way, it is more fitting to be punished than to not suffer evil. For who would not sin by advising the removal of the oil for these things? This is not my word, but the Lord of all says these things when he prevented the prophet from praying for them, saying: 'Do not pray for this people, and do not ask for them to be pitied, and do not approach me for them, for I will not listen.' Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The sons gather wood, and the fathers kindle fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the army of heaven, and they have sown offerings to foreign gods to provoke me. The sons gather wood, the fathers kindle fire, the women knead dough, so that nothing may be found outside of sin. But they who work sin will rightly hear. 'For you have known my back, and I will turn my back on you to not serve me as a priest.'

And they forgot God's law, and I will forget their children. For the manner of punishment is always in proportion to the magnitude of the sins, and it is necessary for those who have sinned to follow the sin in like manner. What would be greater for suffering what they have brought upon themselves, or more grievous for those who have been so greatly deceived, than to be excluded from divine worship and to lose the memory they had from God, through which they had a share of well-being and lived without need? But the deed is a terrible thing, and inaccessible to the foolish. When those who least ought to have it appear to have acquired it, then a pretext for madness is found for those who possess it. The Israelites, having suffered this and having despised the Master's philanthropy, did not want to know the divine law, but rather gave themselves over to all kinds of laziness and eagerly yielded to alien desires, not doing what seemed necessary to the lawgiver, but rather setting their own law according to their own will, and being guided only by their own decrees.
pass_b_english: … They do not deny the novelty of wickedness, but they practice it so shamefully, as if they are superior when they are not caught. They are filled with all kinds of wickedness and bear all uncleanness within themselves, yet they make a pretense of virtue by clinging to the name of fasting alone.

Consider the example of the most ignorant and uneducated Pharisee, whom our Lord Christ describes in the Gospels (Luke 18:11-12) as praying in the temple. This Pharisee boasts about his fasting and tithing, yet he is full of pride and uncleanness within. He is like a whitewashed tomb, beautiful on the outside but full of dead bones and all sorts of uncleanness within (Matthew 23:27).

For they did not want to know the divine law, but also having trampled on the one given to them, they were disobedient and unrepentant. As a result, God reproaches them through the prophet, who cries out in frustration, asking to whom he should speak and testify, since the people's ears are uncircumcised and they are unable to hear. The word of the Lord has become a mockery to them, and they deliberately refuse to listen to it.

For those who sin voluntarily, the advice of what is beneficial is burdensome, and to those who want to live licentiously, self-control is not pleasant. This is similar to the state of those who are drunk, whose minds are confirmed in foolishness, and right thinking is removed. Likewise, those who are conquered by pleasure and have sunk into the depths of sin, having surrendered their sober mind to unclean passions, have evil firmly established within themselves, completely inclined towards it and looking at it, bound by this disease.

From the day your fathers came out of Egypt until this day, I have sent all my servants, the prophets, to you, but they have not listened to me, and they have not given ear, but instead they have stiffened their necks more than their fathers (Jeremiah 7:26). You alone have been shown the evil of your ancestors' deeds, and you have been born in unrighteousness, condemning the weaknesses of the law. You have been given the power to overcome, but you have chosen victory over all shame, and you have been allotted a vote. However, God, the judge of all, condemns you.

The prophet is told to lament the fact that the people have stiffened their necks, and the Lord says that he has rejected and despised the generation that did these things (Jeremiah 7:9-10). The sons of Judah did evil in his sight, setting up abominations in the house that bears his name, and building the altar of Topheth. They even denied their benefactor and considered idolatry more useful, giving sacrifices to the gods they had created for themselves.

Some people, driven by their passions, were devoting their minds to foreign desires, and they would seize the most beautiful mountain groves to offer sacrifices to the demons, invoking the nymphs, as the Greek poets called them, Hamadryads and Oreads. They were shameless in their desires, boasting about their actions, and causing great pain to the lawgiver. The prophet Jeremiah condemned such behavior, saying that the house of Israel had gone up to every high mountain and under every leafy tree to commit fornication, and yet they did not return to me (Jeremiah 3:2).

The Jews' harsh and unyielding choice is a testament to their refusal to be saved, as they always extend towards the worse, not knowing how to be self-controlled. They hate the ways of benefit and do not avoid the time of pleasure, not abstaining from it. This is evident in their failure to guard the beginning and their lack of humility towards the ambition of the Master.

Those who have the opportunity to know and be saved, yet neglect the things that are beneficial and do not consider the great love of humanity, will reasonably condemn themselves. For they have gone beyond all arrogance, having the chance to find release from punishment, but instead they have departed from sin and called upon themselves a heavier punishment, always adding to their transgressions. For who would not sin by advising the removal of the oil for these things? To those who are disposed in this way, it is more fitting to be punished than to not suffer evil.

The Lord of all says these things when he prevented the prophet from praying for them, saying, 'Do not pray for this people, and do not ask for them to be pitied, and do not approach me for them, for I will not listen' (Jeremiah 7:16). The people's sins are evident in their actions, as they provoke the Lord by offering sacrifices to foreign gods. The sons gather wood, the fathers kindle fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the army of heaven, so that nothing may be found outside of sin. They will rightly hear the Lord's judgment, for they have turned their backs on him, and he will turn his back on them, saying, 'For you have known my back, and I will turn my back on you, so that you shall not serve me as a priest. For you have known God's law, and I will forget your children' (Jeremiah 7:11-15).

The Israelites forgot God's law, and as a result, they suffered the consequences of their actions. The manner of punishment is always proportional to the magnitude of the sins committed, and those who have sinned must follow the path of sin in like manner. To be excluded from divine worship and to lose the memory they had from God is a terrible fate, one that is inaccessible to the foolish. The Israelites had been given a share of well-being and had lived without need, but they despised the Master's philanthropy and did not want to know the divine law.

Instead, they gave themselves over to all kinds of laziness and eagerly yielded to alien desires. They did not do what seemed necessary to the lawgiver, but rather set their own law according to their own will, and were guided only by their own decrees. Having such a mindset, they were prone to madness. The deed is a terrible thing, and inaccessible to the foolish. When those who least ought to have it appear to have acquired it, then a pretext for madness is found for those who possess it. The Israelites, having suffered this and having despised the Master's philanthropy, did not want to know the divine law, but rather gave themselves over to all kinds of laziness and eagerly yielded to alien desires, not doing what seemed necessary to the lawgiver, but rather setting their own law according to their own will, and being guided only by their own decrees. …
